written_before: the first GitLab transition of the temporal replication; no GitLab calibration or probe response had been observed at the time of writing
scope: second product only (GitLab 17.11.7); the Gitea record keeps the original 6/6 gate and the original protocol hash

change.calibration_gate: primary vantage 4 of 4 (owner_on_own_private, collaborator_read_on_private, non_collaborator_on_private, owner_self_vantage)
change.secondary_vantage_cells: recorded verbatim as diagnostics; not a pass/fail condition

reason: The base protocol already declares the secondary vantage inadmissible as an oracle (calibration.secondary_vantage_verdict), because a credential that cannot read the surface cannot distinguish 'no grant' from 'no visibility'.
Gating a run on a column that is excluded from every denominator conflates two different things: a product's choice of which endpoints a member may read, and a failure of the entitlement oracle.
The primary vantage carries every scored oracle answer; only it should gate the run.
not_a_weakening: No scored field changes: oracle_answer continues to come from the primary vantage alone, and the abstention, versioning and reporting rules are untouched. The secondary vantage was never used to set E, TP or FP.

product_note.why_the_two_products_differ: Gitea exposes GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{u}/permission, which answers only for a privileged vantage and returns 403/404 to a read collaborator or an outsider. GitLab exposes GET /projects/{id}/members/all/{uid}, whose 200/404 answer is readable by a project member but whose 404 is ambiguous for a caller who cannot see the project at all.
product_note.consequence: The secondary vantage is expected to be one-sided on both products: a positive answer is credible, an absent answer is not a deny. This is recorded as measurement, not as an assumption used for scoring.
